encounters.cc: Bilateral hand numbness and tingling for 6 months, worse at night, with associated fatigue and weight gain.

lines: Bilateral hand numbness and tingling for 6 months, worse at night, with associated fatigue and weight gain.
A 42-year-old female presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of bilateral hand numbness and tingling, particularly in the thumb, index, and middle fingers.
She reports that her symptoms are worse at night and often awaken her from sleep.
She also mentions generalized fatigue, weight gain, and cold intolerance.
Her past medical history is significant for hypothyroidism.
She takes for which she takes levothyroxine.
However, she admits to being non-compliant with her medication over the past year.
- Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol inhaler 250/50 mcg inhaled twice daily
- Albuterol inhaler 90 mcg inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
- Prednisolone acetate ophthalmic suspension 1%, 1 drop in each eye twice daily
Smoking: Former smoker, 10 pack-years, quit 5 years ago.
Alcohol: Social, 1-2 glasses of wine weekly.
On physical examination, you note dry, coarse skin, and delayed relaxation of deep tendon reflexes.
A Tinel's test elicits tingling in her fingers, and a Phalen's test reproduces her symptoms.
Her thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) level is 12 mIU/L (normal range: 0.4-4.0 mIU/L), and her free thyroxine (T4) level is 0.5 ng/dL (normal range: 0.9-1.7 ng/dL).

encounters.cc: Progressively worsening headaches and amenorrhea with bilateral milky nipple discharge over the past 6 months.

lines: Progressively worsening headaches and amenorrhea with bilateral milky nipple discharge over the past 6 months.
The patient returns to the Endocrinology clinic six months following her initial evaluation for hypothyroidism.
Her symptoms began approximately 6 months ago, when she also noticed milky discharge from both breasts.
She denies visual disturbances, but occasionally has trouble reading fine print.
She has no history of pregnancy, and her last menstrual period was over 8 months ago.
Her medical history includes well-controlled hypothyroidism.
- Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol inhaler 250/50 mcg inhaled twice daily
- Albuterol inhaler 90 mcg inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
- Prednisolone acetate ophthalmic suspension 1%, 1 drop in each eye twice daily
Smoking: Former smoker, 10 pack-years, quit 5 years ago.
Alcohol: Social, 1-2 glasses of wine weekly.
Physical examination reveals bitemporal visual field deficits on confrontation testing.
Serum prolactin is elevated at 210 ng/mL. TSH and free T4 are within normal limits.
MRI of the brain reveals a 1.7 cm mass in the sellar region impinging on the optic chiasm.

encounters.cc: Joint pain and morning stiffness lasting over one hour, initially in fingers and progressing to wrists and knees over 6 months.

lines: Joint pain and morning stiffness lasting over one hour, initially in fingers and progressing to wrists and knees over 6 months.
The patient presents to Rheumatology with joint symptoms in the context of established hypothyroidism and prolactinoma.
She reports a 6-month history of joint pain and stiffness, particularly in the mornings lasting more than one hour.
She reports that the symptoms initially started in her fingers and have now progressed to involve her wrists and knees.
- Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol inhaler 250/50 mcg inhaled twice daily
- Albuterol inhaler 90 mcg inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
- Prednisolone acetate ophthalmic suspension 1%, 1 drop in each eye twice daily
Smoking: Former smoker, 10 pack-years, quit 5 years ago.
Alcohol: Social, 1-2 glasses of wine weekly.
She denies any recent infections, diarrhea, or genitourinary symptoms.
On physical examination, there is bilateral swelling and tenderness of the proximal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints.
There is also mild synovitis in both knees.

encounters.cc: Gradually worsening finger stiffness, difficulty opening jars, and persistent dull ache in both wrists for 3 months.

lines: Gradually worsening finger stiffness, difficulty opening jars, and persistent dull ache in both wrists for 3 months.
The patient with rheumatoid arthritis and prior evaluations for hand numbness and joint pain returns for follow-up.
She reports the symptoms are worst in the morning and often make it hard to get dressed, though they improve somewhat over the course of the day.
She also notes that her wedding ring feels tighter than usual and she occasionally feels tingling in her palms.
- Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol inhaler 250/50 mcg inhaled twice daily
- Albuterol inhaler 90 mcg inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
- Prednisolone acetate ophthalmic suspension 1%, 1 drop in each eye twice daily
Smoking: Former smoker, 10 pack-years, quit 5 years ago.
Alcohol: Social, 1-2 glasses of wine weekly.
Physical examination reveals swelling and tenderness at the second and third metacarpophalangeal joints bilaterally, with restricted wrist flexion due to discomfort.
Tinel and Phalen maneuvers reproduce her paresthesias.
Laboratory studies show a normocytic anemia and elevated C-reactive protein.

encounters.cc: Progressive right-sided hearing loss and episodes of vertigo over 6 months with occasional facial numbness.

lines: Progressive right-sided hearing loss and episodes of vertigo over 6 months with occasional facial numbness.

This 47-year-old female with hypothyroidism, prolactinoma, rheumatoid arthritis, and carpal tunnel syndrome presents with a 6-month history of progressive right-sided hearing loss and episodes of vertigo.
She also reports occasional right-sided facial numbness.
She denies otalgia, otorrhea, or ototoxic medication use.
- Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol inhaler 250/50 mcg inhaled twice daily
- Albuterol inhaler 90 mcg inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
- Prednisolone acetate ophthalmic suspension 1%, 1 drop in each eye twice daily
Smoking: Former smoker, 10 pack-years, quit 5 years ago.
Alcohol: Social, 1-2 glasses of wine weekly.
The Weber test lateralizes to the left ear, and the Rinne test indicates air conduction is greater than bone conduction bilaterally.
Cranial nerve examination reveals decreased corneal reflex and facial sensation on the right side.
Audiometry shows sensorineural hearing loss in the right ear.
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain with gadolinium contrast is ordered.

encounters.cc: Painful oral ulcers for 2 months and recent onset of flaccid skin blisters on chest and back that rupture easily.

lines: Painful oral ulcers for 2 months and recent onset of flaccid skin blisters on chest and back that rupture easily.
The patient presents for dermatology follow-up in the context of rheumatoid arthritis and endocrine disorders.
She reports that the oral ulcers began as small vesicles that rapidly progressed to large erosions, making it difficult to eat.
Over the past week, she has noticed similar blisters forming on her chest and back, which easily rupture with minor friction.
Her medical history is significant for hypothyroidism,.
She takes for which she takes levothyroxine.
- Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol inhaler 250/50 mcg inhaled twice daily
- Albuterol inhaler 90 mcg inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
- Prednisolone acetate ophthalmic suspension 1%, 1 drop in each eye twice daily
Smoking: Former smoker, 10 pack-years, quit 5 years ago.
Alcohol: Social, 1-2 glasses of wine weekly.

On physical examination, flaccid bullae are noted on her trunk, and gentle pressure on the edge of an intact blister causes it to extend into the adjacent normal-appearing skin (positive Nikolsky sign).
Several erosions with crusting are also present on her buccal mucosa.
- Complete Blood Count (CBC): Within normal limits
A skin biopsy is performed, and histopathology reveals intraepidermal cleavage with acantholysis.
Direct immunofluorescence of the biopsy specimen shows intercellular deposits of IgG and C3 in the epidermis.

encounters.cc: Progressive shortness of breath with dry cough and increasing fatigue over several months.

lines: Progressive shortness of breath with dry cough and increasing fatigue over several months.
The patient returns for outpatient pulmonology care with a history of rheumatoid arthritis, hypothyroidism, and pemphigus vulgaris.
She reports increasing fatigue and dry cough over the past few months.
She has been compliant with her methotrexate therapy and has not experienced recent joint flares.
She denies chest pain, hemoptysis, or wheezing.
- Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol inhaler 250/50 mcg inhaled twice daily
- Albuterol inhaler 90 mcg inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
- Prednisolone acetate ophthalmic suspension 1%, 1 drop in each eye twice daily
10-pack-year smoking history but quit 5 years ago
Oxygen saturation is 93% on room air
Lung exam reveals fine bibasilar crackles
Chest X-ray reveals reticular opacities at the lung bases
Pulmonary function testing demonstrates a restrictive pattern with decreased DLCO

encounters.cc: Gradually worsening peripheral vision loss in both eyes over 3 months without pain or redness.

lines: Gradually worsening peripheral vision loss in both eyes over 3 months without pain or redness.

The patient is a 49-year-old female with chronic anterior uveitis maintained on long-term topical corticosteroid therapy who returns with a three-month history of gradually worsening bilateral peripheral vision loss.
She reports no eye pain or redness.
Her medical history is significant for moderate persistent asthma.
She also has rheumatoid arthritis and chronic uveitis.
She takes inhaled corticosteroids and occasional oral prednisone during exacerbations. topical glucocorticoid eye drops for the past 6 months.
- Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol inhaler 250/50 mcg inhaled twice daily
- Albuterol inhaler 90 mcg inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
- Prednisolone acetate ophthalmic suspension 1%, 1 drop in each eye twice daily
Smoking: Former smoker, 10 pack-years, quit 5 years ago.
Alcohol: Social, 1-2 glasses of wine weekly.
On examination, visual acuity is 20/25 in both eyes, and there is no evidence of cataract or uveitis.
Tonometry reveals an intraocular pressure of 28 mmHg in the right eye and 27 mmHg in the left eye.
Fundoscopic examination shows increased cup-to-disc ratio bilaterally.
Visual field testing demonstrates bilateral peripheral field loss.
